cards.text: Meet Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, highly regarded by his master and a mighty man of valor. Through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. That's a BIG résumé, friend, but there's a "but" coming.

cards.question: Naaman has the rank, the respect and the victories. What's the one thing working against him?

cards.text: Earlier, bands of Arameans had gone out and taken a young girl from the land of Israel. Now she serves Naaman's wife.

cards.question: The young girl from Israel speaks up to her mistress. Who does she say could cure Naaman of his leprosy?

cards.text: Naaman tells the king of Aram what the girl said. The king says go, and he'll send a letter along.
Off goes Naaman with ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and ten sets of clothing. Friend, Mother Miller bought ME for a QUARTER.

cards.question: The king of Aram sends Naaman with a letter to the king of ___.
True or false: The king of Aram's letter asks the king of Israel to cure Naaman of his leprosy.

cards.text: The king of Israel reads the letter and tears his clothes. He asks, “Am I God, killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper?”

cards.question: The king of Israel is sure the king of Aram is seeking a ___ with him.

cards.text: Elisha the man of God hears that the king tore his clothes. So he sends the king a message: why tear your clothes, just let the man come to me.

cards.question: Elisha says once Naaman comes to him, Naaman will know something. What will he know?

answers.text: That there is a prophet in Israel
That the king of Israel is wise

cards.text: So Naaman comes with his horses and chariots and stands at the door of Elisha's house. That's not a visit, friend. That's a PARADE.

cards.question: True or false: With Naaman at the door, Elisha comes out to meet him in person.

cards.text: Instead, Elisha sends him a messenger, who says, “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”

cards.question: Naaman goes away angry. He says he thought Elisha would surely do something for him. What?

answers.text: Come out and call on the name of the LORD
Ride with him down to the Jordan River
Ask the king of Israel to bless him first

cards.text: Naaman says the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, are better than all the waters of Israel, and he turns and goes away in a rage. Friend, the man brought a whole PARADE for a miracle and got told to go take a bath in somebody ELSE'S river.

cards.question: Naaman's servants come up to him and call him “My father.” What's their point?

answers.text: He'd do a great thing so why not this simple one
The rivers of Damascus are just too far away
The prophet might come out if he waits longer

cards.text: So Naaman goes down and dips himself in the Jordan seven times, just like the man of God said. I bet he counted every single one OUT LOUD.

cards.question: Naaman comes up from the seventh dip in the Jordan. What is his flesh like now?

answers.text: Like the flesh of a little child
Clean except for one small spot

cards.text: Naaman doesn't just go home clean. He and all his attendants go back to the man of God and stand right in front of him.

cards.question: Standing before Elisha, what does Naaman declare he now knows for sure?

answers.text: There is no God in all the earth except in Israel
The waters of Israel are better than any in Aram
Elisha is greater than any king in the world

cards.text: Then Naaman says, “So please accept a gift from your servant.” Remember the cargo, friend: SIX THOUSAND shekels of gold.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha accepts Naaman's gift.

cards.text: Elisha says, “As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.” Naaman keeps urging and Elisha keeps refusing, and me? Somebody offers me free gold, I'm saying yes before he finishes the SENTENCE.

cards.question: Since Elisha won't take the gift, Naaman asks for something to take home instead. What is it?

answers.text: As much soil as two mules can carry
Twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan
Cedar logs from the forests of Lebanon

cards.question: Naaman says he will never again make a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any other god but the ___.

cards.text: Then Naaman says, may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing. When his master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship and leans on Naaman's arm, Naaman bows down there too.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha answers Naaman by telling him to go in peace.

cards.text: Naaman travels a short distance. Back home, Gehazi, Elisha's servant, says his master spared this Aramean by not accepting what he brought.

cards.question: Gehazi borrows his master's line, “As surely as the LORD lives,” and makes a plan. What is it?

answers.text: Run after Naaman and get something from him
Go tell Elisha to take the gift after all
Follow Naaman to make sure he gets home

cards.text: So Gehazi pursues Naaman. When Naaman sees him running, he gets down from his chariot to meet him and asks, “Is everything all right?”

cards.question: Gehazi tells Naaman everything is all right. What does he claim Elisha sent him to say?

answers.text: Give silver and clothing for two young men from the sons of the prophets
Come back to the house so Elisha can bless you and your servants again
Elisha has changed his mind and will take the gold you brought after all

cards.question: True or false: Gehazi asks for one talent of silver, and Naaman insists he take more.

cards.text: Naaman ties up two talents of silver in two bags with two sets of clothing, and two of his servants carry it all ahead of Gehazi. At the hill, Gehazi stores the gifts in the house and sends the men away, like me hiding the broken cookies at the bottom of the box before anybody looks.

cards.question: Gehazi walks in and stands before Elisha, who asks where he's been. What does Gehazi say?

answers.text: He was with the sons of the prophets

cards.question: Elisha isn't fooled. He says his ___ went with Gehazi when Naaman got down from his chariot.

cards.text: Then Elisha asks, “Is this the time to accept money and clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, menservants and maidservants?”

cards.question: Elisha says something will cling to Gehazi and his descendants forever. What is it?

cards.text: And as Gehazi leaves Elisha's presence, he is leprous, as white as snow. Naaman went home clean, and Gehazi walked out with Naaman's leprosy.

findings.problem: The question says the king of Israel is sure the king of Aram is seeking a quarrel. In 2 Kings 5:7 the king only says 'he is seeking a quarrel with me,' right after 'this man expects me to cure a leper.' The text doesn't say whether 'he' is the king of Aram or Naaman, but the card picks one. Reword it to leave this open, for example: 'The king of Israel says he is being sought out for a ___.' Or keep the text's wording: 'seeking a ___ with me.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Come out and call on the name of the LORD,' uses Bible wording. The wrong answers, 'Ride with him down to the Jordan River' and 'Ask the king of Israel to bless him first,' are plain modern wording. Cards 14 and 15 also just established that Elisha didn't come out, so 'come out' points straight to the answer. Make the wrong answers sound the same as the right one, or reword the right answer in plain wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. The first is Elisha's quote. The second is 'Naaman keeps urging and Elisha keeps refusing, and me?' The third is the free-gold joke. Cut it to two sentences, for example by joining the urging and refusing beat to the joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
